rows.source: HSE roof-work safety guidance
rows.verified: Roof work is hazardous because it involves work at height and remains a major source of fatal and serious injury.

rows.source: HSE roof-work safety guidance
rows.verified: Roof work accounts for a substantial share of construction fatalities, with fragile roof materials a particularly important cause.

rows.source: HSE roof-work safety guidance
rows.verified: Roof lights and asbestos-cement sheets can be fragile and may fail without warning.

rows.source: HSE roof-work safety guidance
rows.verified: People killed or injured in roof work include maintenance workers and surveyors as well as trained roofers.

rows.source: HSE roof-work safety guidance
rows.verified: Roof work must be properly planned, supervised and carried out by competent people using suitable equipment.

rows.source: HSE roof-work safety guidance
rows.verified: Roof-work planning should cover new construction, repair, maintenance, cleaning and demolition activities.

rows.source: HSE roof-work safety guidance
rows.verified: Roof ladders are a last-resort option for low-risk, short-duration work and must be industrial grade, in good condition and secured against movement.

rows.source: HSE roof-work safety guidance
rows.verified: A roof ladder should not rely on fragile ridge capping for anchorage, and plans must address fragile surfaces, falling objects and emergency rescue.

rows.source: HSE roof-work safety guidance
rows.verified: Roof-work risk depends on roof pitch and condition, fragility, edges and openings, weather, access, work duration, equipment, falling objects and rescue arrangements.

rows.source: HSE roof-work safety guidance
rows.verified: General planning and control of falls, fragile surfaces, access and rescue during roof work guidance does not prove current conditions or control performance at an individual parcel and does not establish an exact incident, exposure or illness probability.

rows.source: HSE rider-operated lift-truck safety and training guidance
rows.verified: Lift trucks are particularly dangerous and are involved in a significant proportion of workplace-transport accidents.

rows.source: HSE rider-operated lift-truck safety and training guidance
rows.verified: Poor supervision and inadequate operator training are common contributors to lift-truck accidents.

rows.source: HSE rider-operated lift-truck safety and training guidance
rows.verified: Operators must receive training to the standard described in the L117 Approved Code of Practice, including occasional users.

rows.source: HSE rider-operated lift-truck safety and training guidance
rows.verified: Operator training should include basic training, specific job training and familiarisation training.

rows.source: HSE rider-operated lift-truck safety and training guidance
rows.verified: Basic and specific job training should normally take place away from production pressure, while familiarisation occurs on the job under close supervision.

rows.source: HSE rider-operated lift-truck safety and training guidance
rows.verified: Trainees should be continuously assessed and pass practical and theoretical testing before being authorised.

rows.source: HSE rider-operated lift-truck safety and training guidance
rows.verified: Trained operators should be monitored and may need retesting or refresher training after unsafe practice, an accident, a long absence or a change in work.

rows.source: HSE rider-operated lift-truck safety and training guidance
rows.verified: Supervisors must understand lift-truck risks and recognise unsafe practice, and visiting drivers or contractors should operate trucks only when adequately trained and familiar with site risks.

rows.source: HSE rider-operated lift-truck safety and training guidance
rows.verified: Lift-truck risk depends on truck type and attachment, load, stability, speed, routes, pedestrians, surface and slopes, maintenance, supervision and operator competence.

rows.source: HSE rider-operated lift-truck safety and training guidance
rows.verified: General operator competence, staged training, supervision, monitoring and safe use of lift trucks guidance does not prove current conditions or control performance at an individual parcel and does not establish an exact incident, exposure or illness probability.
